correctness.rationale: For a nontrivial directed path, the eventual index of the power sequence is at least two, so the first power cannot equal any higher power and no higher power can generate it. Otherwise the partial map is a permutation on its domain and has exactly φ(o) generators of the same embedded ambient-unital cyclic submonoid, whether or not its local identity is the ambient identity. This includes the empty map and order one. Weighting each element by the reciprocal of its multiplicity gives Q_n−H_n+W_n with W_n the displayed totient sum. Independent direct enumeration of powers gave 2,7,33,198,1448 for n=1,…,5; a separate exact formula evaluation gave 12526 at n=6. For a uniform permutation of m points, the expected number of vertices in cycles of length at most J is J, so the largest cycle is at most J with probability ≤J/m. Since the order is at least the largest cycle and φ(v)≥sqrt(v/2), taking J=⌊m^(2/3)⌋ shows the mean reciprocal totient and probability of multiplicity one tend to zero. At defect j the local permutation count is n!/j!; the summable factorial tail gives W_n=o(n!), Q_n−M_n∼e n!, and the same equivalent for the number of event elements, but not an exact equality with the deficit. Dividing fixed-defect event counts by the latter equivalent proves the conditional Poisson(1) law. Finally Q_n/n!=L_n(−1). Against the Bessel weights n^k/(k!)², the ratio of successive weights concentrates k/√n at 1; on that scale (n)_k/n^k tends to e^(−1/2) by logarithmic expansion. Laplace's method for the Bessel integral gives e^(2√n)/(2√π n^(1/4)), establishing the stated constant.

Elliott–Levine–Mitchell and adjacent Resultary census statements
value.rationale: The exact embedded census addresses a natural distinction from abstract classification. More substantially, the theorem quantifies when uniform generators fail to identify their power submonoids, giving a sharp constant for a stretched-exponentially rare event and the limiting rank defect conditional on that event. The factorial law reveals where collisions occur in a way the total count or a uniqueness-with-high-probability statement cannot.
residual_risks: The exact count alone is a short structural corollary; the assessment of value rests also on the distinct probabilistic conclusions.
